newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine grain buyers waiting for soft prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippine grain buyers waiting for soft prices.

text.p: Philippine grain importers said on Friday they were waiting for prices of corn and wheat to drop before resuming their shopping.
Local importers stayed out of the market this week due to high prices.
"We are waiting for U.S. wheat prices to drop below $180 per tonne," said one executive in a Philippine flour mill.
Philippine flour millers bought around 1.3 million tonnes of wheat, mostly U.S. wheat, at an average $200 per tonne FOB in the first half of the year.
"This comprises 70 percent of the projected Philippine wheat requirement for 1997," said one senior trader.
U.S. wheat are currently pegged at an average $180 per tonne FOB.
Corn importers are also waiting for prices to soften.
A group of Philippine feed millers planned to buy about 50,000 tonnes of yellow corn at $120 per tonne C&F, an executive in one of the firms said.
U.S. corn prices are now hovering at $128 per tonne C&F, the executive said.
The Philippines has so far bought at least 245,000 tonnes U.S. and Chinese yellow corn, a senior trader said.
Corn shortage in the country this year was earlier forecast by industry executives to reach at least one million tonnes.
Corn deliveries on orders made by local firms this year are expected to arrive over the weekend.

MV Sammi Manna, carrying 23,000 tonnes Chinese yellow corn, is scheduled to arrive at the Bataan grains terminal on July 6. The cargo included 10,000 tonnes bought last month by Swift Foods Inc from Louis Dreyfus at $138 per tonne C&F.

Another ship, MV Ermis, is also scheduled to arrive in the same terminal on July 22 to deliver 55,000 tonnes of U.S. corn bought by a group of feed millers and hog raisers at $137.75 per tonne C&F from Continental Grains.
Meanwhile, soymeal importers are expected to remain in the sidelines due to ample supply.
The country has so far imported 700,000 tonnes of soymeal or 80 percent of the country's requirement this year, said one trader.
